name: Lenskart Solutions Ltd
title: Lenskart Solutions Ltd - 544600 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Lenskart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 41% YoY to ₹2,516 crore, with reported EBITDA up 61% and pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at 12.8%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter since listing: revenue grew 41% YoY to ₹2,516 crore, PAT reached ₹204 crore, and EBITDA margin expanded 2.7 pp to 21.3%. India and international both grew, with India same-store sales growth at 24% and international revenue up 35.4%. FY26 crossed ₹1,700 crore EBITDA, ₹1,000 crore pre-Ind AS EBITDA and ₹500 crore PAT for the first time. Management kept the steady-state pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at about 25% and guided FY27 net store additions to roughly FY26 levels (542 in India plus 61 international in FY26).

financial_highlights.change: Q4 from 8.1% YoY; FY26 from 3.6% in FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash (ex IPO-related payables, largely settled in April)
Return on capital employed (ex undeployed IPO proceeds)

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,475 crore (+44% YoY) with eyewear units up 24.3% to 7.9 million; product margin held at 64%. Store count 2,609 after 170 net adds in Q4 and 542 in FY26; FY26 pre-Ind AS EBITDA ₹753 crore at 14.3% margin.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,054 crore (+35.4% YoY; +25% constant currency) with eyewear units up 29%. Store count 718 after 13 net adds in Q4 and 61 in FY26; FY26 pre-Ind AS EBITDA ₹264 crore at 7% margin. Japan was the strongest market; Middle East had a temporary traffic dip that has recovered to near normal.

guidance_outlook: Net new store additions in FY27 expected to be around FY26 levels (FY26: 542 India, 61 international).
Long-term steady-state pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin unchanged at approximately 25% (India currently 14-15%, about 10 pp runway).
Quarterly margins will vary with store-opening phasing, seasonality and long-term bets; management said it will prioritise long-term value over short-term linearity.
Management urged investors to track trailing 12-month volume growth as the cleanest measure of underlying demand.
Step-up in R&D spend in FY27 for automated eye testing, smart eyewear (B by Lenskart) and AI; FY27 priorities include scaling to 100 million customers.
capex_capacity: FY26 store capex funded 603 net new stores (ops cash flow ₹887 crore), alongside manufacturing investment including the new Hyderabad facility.
Factory floors to move toward near full automation from the current 75%; Bhiwadi centralised facility supports next-day delivery across 78 cities (from 7 cities initially, about 30 later).
Hyderabad plant and Thailand JV cited as structural answers to reduce import dependence.
Remote optometry stores rose 3.7x in a year to 623.
India eyewear units reached 29 million in FY26 (18 million two years earlier); long-term store runway of 4,500 stores in India previously articulated, management said more is possible.
demand_pricing: India same-store sales growth 24% in Q4 (broad-based across Metro, Tier 1, Tier 2); same-pincode sales growth 31%. Management declined to split SSSG into value and volume; it rejected an analyst's estimate of ~10% volume SSS as too low.
Eye tests: 6.8 million globally in Q4 (+45% YoY); India eye tests 6 million (+50%); about half of India eye tests were first-time exams. Gold active members 8.8 million (+29.5%).
Product margin in India held at 64% despite rupee depreciation; management said structural margin gains were offset by currency (RMB 11 to 14 cited as an example).
ASP fluctuations are driven by OPP campaigns (New Lens Replacement, Hustlr) and by upgrades to Own days, Meller, progressives.
International ACP reduction ongoing as markets are integrated into central supply chain; operating leverage seen after scale in Singapore, Dubai and now Japan.
Meller sunglasses out of stock in all markets; launched in 1,000+ India stores, Middle East and Southeast Asia, with Japan next.

qa_highlights.question: What geopolitical, raw material, China-sourcing or market risks should investors monitor?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight and raw material have had no meaningful impact so far; currency is the biggest variable. 42% of business is international and vertical integration has offset rupee-import headwinds. No material demand impact seen in India or abroad; Middle East dip was small and brief.

qa_highlights.question: How was the India gross margin held near 64% in a low-ASP quarter, and does SSSG of ~25% with ~15% price imply ~10% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gains came from vertical integration and process changes, not price increases; OPP campaigns are paired with upgrades to offset margin. Management said the 10% volume estimate was not correct and that volume SSS is meaningfully higher; it does not disclose value/volume split.

qa_highlights.question: How will employee productivity and cost leverage trend, especially internationally?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage came mainly from SSG and volume growth on a fixed cost base. HQ and tech costs were flat as headcount was not added; AI and remote optometry are expected to add more output per person.

qa_highlights.question: Does Tier 2 strength expand the 4,500-store runway and allow faster expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than 4,500 stores are possible; 200+ Tier 2 stores have been added and feed GeoIQ. Metros are also growing (eye tests +45%+) and are the main source of SSG.

qa_highlights.question: How should we think about competition in smart glasses (e.g. Google re-entry)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the category is very early with no clear form-factor winner; it sees Lenskart's role in prescription and distribution of smart glasses and its app/data layer as advantages. Launch focus is on learning, not near-term sales.

qa_highlights.question: How will international margins converge to India's level, and what is the KSA breakeven status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a quarter for reaching 15% international margin; it cited falling ACP and operating leverage after scale. KSA is about two years old and ahead of where UAE was at the same stage; no breakeven date was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will store expansion focus on saturating existing pincodes or entering new ones, and what about cannibalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Site selection is bottom-up using mobility data within a 10-minute travel radius, not pincode-level. Management said stores tripled in many cities while revenue doubled, and that much of SSG came from multi-store pincodes.

qa_highlights.question: Is same-day delivery a near-term target and does the store network become an inventory model?
qa_highlights.answer: No delivery target set; same-day is in experiments in Singapore and some Indian markets. Stores are being used as micro-fulfilment nodes for OTC products and at-home frame trials, which management described as a chemist model rather than a warehouse.

qa_highlights.question: What is Meller's traction and scale target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Meller is ahead of plan, sold out across markets, and is being positioned as a Gentle Monster-type brand for Gen Z. No specific scale target was given.

risks_watch: Rupee depreciation: currency is the largest variable on imported product cost; India product margin held at 64% only because of vertical integration and premiumisation.
Quarterly margin volatility from store-opening phasing and OPP-led ASP dilution; management has deliberately deferred linear margin delivery.
International margin ramp (FY26 7%) depends on scale in newer markets such as KSA, which is not yet at EBITDA breakeven.
Metro eye-test wait times and conversion from eye tests (~50% growth) to eyewear volume (~25%) are open execution items.
Smart-glasses competition (e.g., Google re-entry) and heavy R&D step-up in FY27 may pressure near-term margins.
Middle East demand dip was temporary, but geopolitical disruption remains a stated watch item.
Management did not disclose SSSG split between value and volume, which limits external modelling.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margin trajectory and long-term runway, with an explicit preference for long-term value over quarterly linearity. Evasive on quantitative detail: declined to split SSSG into value and volume, gave no timeline for international margin to reach India's level, and gave no KSA breakeven date or same-day delivery target.
key_quotes: Revenue grew 41% year-on-year to ₹2,516 crores, our strongest quarter as a public company.
We urge investors to track trailing 12-month volume growth as the cleanest measure of underlying market expansion.
Our long-term steady-state EBITDA pre-Ind AS margin expectation remains unchanged to approximately 25%.
The compounding effect of revenue and margin will continue, but we will always prioritize action for long-term value creation over short-term linearity.

adds.what: FY27 net new store additions around FY26 levels (FY26: 542 India + 61 international)

growth.why: No explicit FY27 revenue growth figure guided; management guided FY27 net store additions around FY26 levels (542 India, 61 international), backed by store capex and the Bhiwadi/Hyderabad manufacturing build-out, while Q4 revenue grew 41% YoY with India SSSG at 24%.
